Leaf walks out in the open and takes a deep breath of evening air. She smiles, proud of herself for going into a bar for the first time, before her goblin eyes suddenly shine with recollection. She reaches into her dress pocket and pulls out the berry her friend Gill had given her the day before. After looking around for a promising spot, preferably away from too much foot traffic, Leaf sits cross legged on the ground and digs a hole in the dirt, before gently placing the now shriveled berry in the hole and covering it back up. She bends over and places her face close to the ground and says, "May the Wild Mother and her patrons help you grow big and strong, so that someday after I've explored the new world, I can come visit you in the old one." The ground glows softly as the berry sprouts from the dirt. She sits here silently tending to the dirt and breathing in the fresh air for a bit, content with her new life.

The night’s clouds part, and the moonlight is bright, casting the world in hues of purple and blue, in diminishing greys and in this moment you remember that this place was once wild.


A wolf howls. It's too close to be outside of the city. As your mind passively searches for the source, and the goosebumps begin to rise on your arms, the howl is returned by a chorus of dozens. Lights can be seen dancing. Small and yellow. No. Not lights. Eyes. Eyes of beasts running through the cobblestone streets and atop tiled roofs. 


A wolf stops in front of you about 100 yards out. It is smallish and grey, with eyes surely analyzing you yet fearless in nature. It lets out a billowing howl and you feel the primal cry in the core of you, the force of it giving meaning to instincts long dormant in humanoid species.
